answer: Each agent earns a reputation score that rises with continuous task fulfillment, recorded on an immutable ledger that timestamps contributions like milestones on a terrace overlooking the network. When an identity stalls, its reputation decays toward the nadir at a fixed rate, and any new node must purchase a baseline score equal to the cost of a comet‑size stake, making mass creation economically prohibitive. An attacker therefore spends linear tokens per fake ID plus ongoing decay penalties, quickly outweighing any gain.
